Theme

School & learning · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

learn verb

study, be taught

also learn to, learn how to, be taught

classical

Cic. Sen. 26: litterās Graecās senex didicī
Plaut. Aul. 595: puerī quī nāre discunt
Traupman 30

discō, discere, didicī

verb, third conjugation

With an accusative (litterās discere), an infinitive for a skill (nāre discere, learn to swim), and ab or ex aliquō for the teacher. No supine in classical Latin. To learn by heart is ēdiscere (see learn by heart).

Other words

  • perdiscō, perdiscere, perdidicī — learn thoroughly

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.69: hic locus dē vītā et mōribus tōtus est ōrātōrī perdiscendus

    Lewis & Short: “rare but class.”.

Examples

  • Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt, alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus

    The boys love each other and play games, but they learn: one needs the reins, the other the spurs.Cic. Att. 6.1.12

  • aestāte puerī sī valent, satis discunt

    In summer, if children keep well, they learn enough.Mart. 10.62.12

  • alius ait hoc mē prīmum docē, item alius hoc volō, inquit, discere, istud nōlō

    One says, “Teach me this first”; another, “I want to learn this,” he says, “not that.”Gell. 1.9.9

  • hoc ante omnia fac, mī Lūcīlī: disce gaudēre

    Above all, my Lucilius, do this: learn to be glad.Sen. Ep. 23.3

See also learn by heart, lesson, school, teacher, homework, read, learn.
